A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Mixture of Contexts for Long Video Generation. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including material moved or renumbered between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation comparisons, efficiency measurements, component ablations and zero-shot qualitative results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and reports an expanded regularization ablation in Appendix D, Table 4.

M1.justification: Content-aligned top-k routing, mandatory text and intra-shot links, causal masking, context drop-off/drop-in and outer-loop routing already appear in v1. The attention-sink explanation and expanded regularization ablation do not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions cover short single-shot generation, minute-long multi-shot generation, zero-shot sparsification and the Wan-2.1-1.3B experiment using Vchitect data. Moving the short-video and zero-shot studies does not change coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the native 3B MMDiT baseline, LCT, dense-attention Wan and FlashAttention 2. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines; Table 4 extends ablations of MoC itself.

E3.justification: Table 4 adds an explicit regularization-on/off comparison with both forced links enabled. This extends the evaluation design, while retaining the stated chunk size, top-k, training budget and metrics. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The forced-link ablation in v1 Appendix B becomes a forced-link plus context drop-in/out ablation in v2 Appendix D. It newly tests the regularizer's contribution with both links enabled. Chunk-size/top-k, causality and zero-shot analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The expanded ablation continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 4 retains its first three numerical rows but replaces v1's both-links row with separate regularization-off/on results. Dynamic Degree is 0.5654 in the old row versus 0.4844 and 0.5469 in the new rows; other metrics also differ. v1 leaves that row's regularization status unspecified, preventing a same-setting performance comparison. Other tables and matched figures retain their results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, the causal-routing argument and the outer-loop routing formulation are unchanged. The added attention-sink discussion is conceptual explanation rather than a new mathematical definition, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The conclusion narrows its statement about avoiding heuristics from avoiding fixed-rule selection generally to avoiding Field-of-View selection specifically. The central claims about learned retrieval, minute-scale memory, sparsity and speedup remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 newly interprets mandatory text links as attention sinks that stabilize attention and gradient flow. Appendix D extends the performance interpretation to context drop-in/out and connects stability to attention sinks and MoBA. The limitations paragraph removes the suggested extension to video-world-model datasets.

D1.justification: Table 4 newly identifies context drop-in/out as disabled in the three numerically unchanged forced-link configurations, clarifying a previously unspecified setting. Training schedules, hardware, implementation details, Wan settings and project access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds LaCT, VMem and the attention-sinks paper, connecting existing components to these research directions. Section 4 also newly describes LCT as the only available architecture for general-scene long multi-shot generation. These are limited positioning updates; the LCT venue update alone is bibliographic.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative now foregrounds long multi-shot generation, moving the existing short-video study into Appendix B and placing zero-shot evaluation first in the appendix. Selected headings and explanations are revised, and an LLM writing-use disclosure is added. Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The same six figures and five tables are retained, with relocation, renumbering and some resizing. The short-video table and figure move to the appendix. Table 4 gains a regularization column and expands from four to five result rows.

improvement.justification: The expanded Table 4 makes an existing regularizer's contribution assessable, and the attention-sink explanation better motivates and positions mandatory text links. These modestly strengthen evidence and clarity. The new ablation shows consistency and motion gains alongside small aesthetic/image-quality losses; its relationship to v1's replaced row remains unexplained, while the core benchmark evidence is unchanged.
